claims.claim: A MetaFilter reader disputes the ambiguity reading, arguing Wolfe's unreliability is a puzzle readers assemble from careful cluing rather than genuine epistemic uncertainty.
claims.quote: assemble based on careful cluing the truth that the narrator doesn't know

claims.claim: A MetaFilter reader says the text reveals how horrible Severian is through what still manages to slip through his own narration.
claims.quote: revealing how horrible he is through what still manages to slip

claims.claim: A MetaFilter reader says some Wolfe narrators are sincere recorders of what they experienced who have fundamentally misunderstood the events they record.
claims.quote: sincere recorders of the truth they've experienced, but they've fundamentally misunderstood

claims.claim: A MetaFilter reader names deliberate frustration of expectations as the Wolfe device more central than unreliable narration.
A MetaFilter reader states that in The Book of the New Sun everything archaic to Severian is rendered as Latin.
claims.quote: Everything archaic to Severian is rendered as Latin.

claims.claim: A MetaFilter reader attributes to Wolfe the remark that everything means something but not everything means very much.
claims.source: MetaFilter user “straight” relaying Gene Wolfe, thread 149475, 8 May 2015
claims.quote: Everything means something, but not everything means very much.

claims.feature: other: counter-evidence, anomaly as authorial error
claims.claim: A MetaFilter reader reports that Wolfe, asked by letter about a contradiction in the first pages of Shadow of the Torturer, answered that it was a typo.
claims.source: MetaFilter user “Ipsifendus” reporting a letter from Gene Wolfe, thread 149475, 8 May 2015, 9:25 AM

claims.claim: Ian Sales says the title novella of The Fifth Head of Cerberus opens traditionally, as a childhood memory.
claims.source: Ian Sales (“iansales”), SFF Chronicles thread 11050, 13 June 2006
claims.quote: The novella opens traditionally enough—a childhood memory

claims.claim: Ian Sales says that three paragraphs after that conventional opening the reader learns the narrator's father traded in children.
claims.source: Ian Sales (“iansales”), SFF Chronicles thread 11050, 13 June 2006
claims.quote: three paragraphs later we learn that the narrator’s father traded in children

claims.claim: Ian Sales says the novella 'V.R.T.' consists of excerpts from taped interviews and a field journal, framed by a military officer reading those documents to decide on an incarceration.
claims.source: Ian Sales (“iansales”), SFF Chronicles thread 11050, 13 June 2006
claims.quote: It consists of excerpts from taped interviews, the field journal

claims.claim: Ian Sales says the authorities read a table of bullet-drop figures found in a field guide as meaning Marsch is an assassin.
claims.source: Ian Sales (“iansales”), SFF Chronicles thread 11050, 13 June 2006
claims.quote: the authorities take this to mean Marsch is an assassin

claims.claim: Ian Sales says clues in the text, including a library shelf description, suggest the unnamed narrator's surname is Wolfe.
claims.source: Ian Sales (“iansales”), SFF Chronicles thread 11050, 13 June 2006
claims.quote: Clues in the text suggest his surname is Wolfe

claims.claim: A forum analyst says objective outside detail is, in his opinion, at the heart of getting to the bottom of things in Wolfe.
claims.source: SFF Chronicles user “felicibusbrevis”, thread 11050, 24 March 2013 (an analysis written for the Urth mailing list)
claims.quote: at the heart of getting to the bottom of things in Wolfe

claims.claim: The same forum analyst says the embedded aboriginal myth “A Story” is written in a mythic dream prose very different from the first part of the novel.
claims.quote: mythic but confusing dream prose that channels the savage mind

claims.claim: A reader of Peace reports taking things in at face value and failing to catch the significance of what Wolfe was alluding to.
claims.source: SFF Chronicles user “Fried Egg”, thread 528814, 14 September 2010
claims.quote: taking things in at face value and failed to catch the significance
